cases.preconditions: frob is built from the merged master revision (go build ./... succeeds; UpperWord implemented via strings.ToUpper, WordSize returns the UTF-8 byte length); the argument is passed verbatim as a single argv entry in a UTF-8 environment.
cases.steps: Run the frob program with argv ['naïve'] (i.e. frob naïve); capture stdout, stderr and the exit code.
cases.oracle: Exit code is 0 and stdout is exactly the single line 'frob: NAÏVE bytes=6' followed by one newline: the word is Unicode-uppercased (ï becomes Ï, proving non-ASCII simple case mapping is applied rather than the placeholder that returns input unchanged) and N=6 is the UTF-8 byte count of 'naïve' (n,a,v,e are 1 byte each, ï is 2). No other stdout output appears.

cases.preconditions: frob is built from the merged master revision; UpperWord implemented via strings.ToUpper.
cases.steps: Run the frob program with argv ['hello']; capture stdout, stderr and the exit code.
cases.oracle: Exit code is 0 and stdout is exactly 'frob: HELLO bytes=5' followed by one newline; all lowercase ASCII letters are uppercased (the placeholder UpperWord that returns the input unchanged would print 'frob: hello bytes=5' and must fail this oracle).

cases.preconditions: frob is built from the merged master revision; the empty string is passed as one argv entry (frob '').
cases.steps: Run the frob program with argv [''] (a single empty argument); capture stdout, stderr and the exit code.
cases.oracle: Exit code is 0 and stdout is exactly 'frob:  bytes=0' followed by one newline, with two spaces between 'frob:' and 'bytes=0' because UpperWord of the empty word is the empty string; UpperWord('',...) must not inject any placeholder or error text.

cases.preconditions: frob is built from the merged master revision; the program is invoked with no argument after the program name.
cases.steps: Run the frob program with an empty argv after the program name; capture stdout, stderr and the exit code.
cases.oracle: Exit code is non-zero (the baseline entry exits 2), a usage message ('usage: frob <word>') appears on stderr, and stdout contains no line starting with 'frob: ' — UpperWord is never observable for a missing word.

cases.preconditions: frob is built from the merged master revision (WordSize implemented to return the UTF-8 byte length); UTF-8 argv passthrough.
cases.steps: Run the frob program with argv ['日本']; capture stdout, stderr and the exit code.
cases.oracle: Exit code is 0 and stdout is exactly 'frob: 日本 bytes=6' followed by one newline: '日本' has 2 runes but 6 UTF-8 bytes (3 per rune), so N=6 proves WordSize counts bytes, not runes or the placeholder 0; the UPPER field equals the input because these runes have no case mapping, isolating WordSize.

cases.preconditions: frob is built from the merged master revision; UTF-8 argv passthrough.
cases.steps: Run the frob program with argv ['é']; capture stdout, stderr and the exit code.
cases.oracle: Exit code is 0 and stdout is exactly 'frob: É bytes=2' followed by one newline: a single rune occupying 2 UTF-8 bytes, so N=2 (not 1) confirms byte-length semantics for the smallest multi-byte input.

cases.preconditions: frob is built from the merged master revision; the empty string is passed as one argv entry.
cases.steps: Run the frob program with argv ['']; capture stdout, stderr and the exit code.
cases.oracle: Exit code is 0 and stdout is exactly 'frob:  bytes=0' followed by one newline: WordSize('') returns 0, distinguishing the implemented function from the placeholder that returned 0 for every input when combined with case QA-AC002-01.

cases.preconditions: frob is built from the merged master revision; the program is invoked with no argument.
cases.steps: Run the frob program with an empty argv after the program name; capture stdout, stderr and the exit code.
cases.oracle: Exit code is non-zero (the baseline entry exits 2), usage appears on stderr, and stdout contains no 'frob: ' line — WordSize is never invoked/observable when the word is missing.

cases.preconditions: frob is built from the merged master revision combining both slices (UpperWord and WordSize wired in frob.go); UTF-8 argv passthrough.
cases.steps: Run the frob program with argv ['héLLo']; capture stdout, stderr and the exit code.
cases.oracle: Exit code is 0 and stdout is exactly 'frob: HÉLLO bytes=6' followed by one newline and nothing else: the combined output of UpperWord (héLLo → HÉLLO, é is 2 UTF-8 bytes so the input is 6 bytes) and WordSize (6) on one line, byte-for-byte.

cases.preconditions: frob is built from the merged master revision; the empty string is passed as one argv entry (frob '').
cases.steps: Run the frob program with argv ['']; capture stdout, stderr and the exit code.
cases.oracle: Exit code is 0 and stdout is exactly 'frob:  bytes=0' followed by one newline (two spaces between 'frob:' and 'bytes=0'), byte-for-byte the specified empty-word combined output; the empty argument is treated as the word, not as a missing argument.

cases.preconditions: frob is built from the merged master revision; the program is invoked with no argument.

cases.oracle: Exit code is non-zero and stdout contains no line starting with 'frob: ' — in particular neither 'frob: --UNKNOWN-FLAG bytes=14' (the known baseline-gap output that treats the flag as the word) nor 'frob: HELLO bytes=5'; a rejection/usage message may appear on stderr but the frob: output line must not be produced on any stream.

cases.oracle: Exit code is non-zero and stdout contains no line starting with 'frob: ' — the unknown flag is rejected even when the accompanying word is empty, so the empty-word success path 'frob:  bytes=0' must not be reached.

development.summary: Repaired adjudicated problem sha256:5ad1563e2da7d5ea1fedd6e3737ffdf13eda6de8c19bb183e0a14b8d275d4ce1 (AC-004 unknown-flag rejection, master-merge responsibility, authorized as in-run frob.go rework). frob.go now checks the first argument with isFlag(): a dash-prefixed argument longer than '-' is an unknown flag (frob defines no flags) and is rejected by the same path as a missing argument — 'usage: frob <word>' on stderr and exit 2 — so no 'frob: ' line is ever emitted for flag invocations, while normal words, the empty word and the missing-argument path behave unchanged. uppercase.go and size.go are untouched. The repair is small and completed in this turn; no batching (granularityReview) needed.
